candidate.falsifier: Any row with nonpositive sigma margin, signed budget ratio at least 1, or mismatch from lambda_phi would falsify this finite algebraic checkpoint.
candidate.mechanism: Replace an absolute adverse-z ceiling by the row's available main-term sigma budget.  The exact finite relation is signed_budget_ratio = -iid_z / budget = lambda_phi, and positivity is signed_budget_ratio < 1.
candidate.name: four-modulus positivity sigma budget
candidate.prediction: Rows may violate a fixed z<3 shortcut but still have large positive sigma margin because the local main term supplies a larger sigma budget.
candidate.smallest_test: Replay the initial and far-lift variance-scale receipts and compute budget, margin, and budget-ratio fields without new prime-orbit recomputation.

decision: The fixed adverse-z cap is the wrong theorem target: it has finite failures.  The useful finite invariant is the positivity budget ratio, which is just lambda_phi in variance-scale coordinates.  On the combined 232 checked rows it remains below 1 with numerical-zero reconstruction of the lambda relation, so the next theorem target is a signed estimate proving lambda_phi<1, equivalently adverse z below the row's growing main-term sigma budget.  This is finite algebraic evidence only; Goldbach remains open.

formula.lambda_equivalence: signed_budget_ratio equals lambda_phi up to floating error

status_boundary: finite q286-WBSS four-modulus positivity-budget audit only; algebraic normalization of existing finite receipts, no independence theorem, fixed-modulus equidistribution theorem, q286 threshold theorem, strict-central Goldbach theorem, or Goldbach proof
